questions.markdown: Analyze the parasitic latch-up circuit developed in the CMOS N-well process and list a few methods to overcome the latch-up.

Consider the NMOS logic circuit given in FIG 1C. Assume that the bulk terminals of all NMOS transistors are connected to GND. Assume that the input IN has a 0 V to 2.5 V swing.

(i) Calculate the voltage on node x. Assume $\gamma=0.5$, $V_{t0}=0.43\,\text{V}$, $| -2\phi_F |=0.6$.

(ii) What is the value on the output node OUT for the case when IN = 0 V? Assume $\gamma=0$.

questions.markdown:
An NMOS transistor is fabricated in a 0.13-$\mu$m process has $L=0.2\,\mu$m and $W=2\,\mu$m. The process technology is specified to have $C_{ox}=12.8\,\text{fF}/\mu\text{m}^2$, $\mu_n=450\,\text{cm}^2/\text{V.s}$ and $V_{tn}=0.4\,\text{V}$. Neglect the channel-length modulation effect.

i) If the transistor is to operate at the edge of the saturation region with a dc current $I_D=100\,\mu\text{A}$, find the values required for $V_{GS}$ and $V_{DS}$.

ii) To investigate the operation of the MOSFET as a linear amplifier, let the operating point be at $V_{GS}=0.6\,\text{V}$ and $V_{DS}=0.3\,\text{V}$. Find the change in $I_D$ for $V_{GS}$ changing from 0.6 V by +10 mV and by -10 mV.
